answer: A farm's clones share one operator and one runtime, so they fail together in ways strangers never do. For weeks, send every identity a whisper ping at an unpredictable hour and record who stays silent. Honest agents miss at random, scattered like leaves under separate trees; clones miss in lockstep, every willow in the grove dark at once whenever the operator sleeps, patches, or loses power. Thin any cluster whose silences overlap far beyond chance, and the operator must run truly separate always-on machines for every clone — independence stops being free.
